name: workflow-resume
description: Find recent dynamic workflow runs that lost agents to API errors, and resume or finish them correctly. A workflow agent that hits a rate limit, usage limit, dropped connection or 5xx returns null with zero retries; parallel()/pipeline() map that to null too, the generated script's closing .filter(Boolean) drops it, and the run reports `completed` with the loss unreported. This skill separates the two shapes that need opposite handling: a finished run with dead agents, and a run that is still live (which must not be relaunched, and whose worktrees and pid-held locks must not be touched). Bundles a stdlib-only read-only scanner that reads the journal and per-agent transcripts rather than the snapshot, because a snapshot is written once at completion and is absent or stale for any live or resumed run; it reports run id, session id and whether that session is still alive, the scriptPath and args needed to resume, journal started/results counts, and each agent's item, state and error. Encodes the mechanics verified from the claude 2.1.220 bundle: the journal is filed under <SESSION-UUID>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/ so a changed session id cold-starts a resume silently (anthropics/claude-code#65796, open) and the fix is a cp -R relocation; the cache key is a sha256 chain over (previous key, prompt, normalised opts) with a sticky miss flag, so replay is a prefix and a run that failed early recovers almost nothing; and the /workflows `r` key only aborts a live AbortController, so a failed agent cannot be retried there. Also carries the reconciliation discipline that matters most in practice: cached results are what an agent said, not what landed, and runs have reported items merged whose branches were still tens of commits ahead of main, so branch ancestry and worktree state decide whether a failed item is resumed in place or re-run clean.
